source.author: verg
source.text: Ille etiam exstincto miseratus Caesare Romam, cum caput obscura nitidum ferrugine texit inpiaque aeternam timuerunt saecula noctem.
source.text_original: Ille etiam exstincto miseratus Caesare Romam, / cum caput obscura nitidum ferrugine texit / inpiaque aeternam timuerunt saecula noctem.
source.text_english: He too, pitying Rome when Caesar was extinguished, covered his shining head with murky gloom, and the impious ages feared an everlasting night.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quando enim interfecto Pharaone, sive dracone sol, et luna, et stellae non dederunt lumen suum, et coelum opertum est tenebris, juxta illud poeticum: Impiaque aeternam timuerunt saecula noctem.
reuse.text_original: Quando enim interfecto Pharaone, sive dracone sol, et luna, et stellae non dederunt lumen suum, et coelum opertum est tenebris, juxta illud poeticum: Impiaque aeternam timuerunt saecula noctem.
reuse.text_english: For when Pharaoh, or the dragon, was slain, the sun and the moon and the stars did not give their light, and the heaven was covered with darkness, according to that poetic line: And the impious ages feared an eternal night.
